problemStatement.informal: Can [ℚ(∛3):ℚ] = 3 be derived as a corollary of the Eisenstein criterion proof for ∛3 irrationality?

insights: adjoin_nthRoot_finrank from CubeRoot2IrrationalOQ03 provides a one-line proof: specializing n=3, m=3, p=3 gives [ℚ(∛3):ℚ] = 3 immediately
minpoly.eq_X_sub_C gives: if α = algebraMap K L a, then minpoly K α = X - C a (degree 1)
Irrationality follows from degree > 1: q ∈ ℚ implies minpoly = X - C q (degree 1), contradicting minpoly degree 3
General principle: algebraic α has [ℚ(α):ℚ] > 1 iff α ∉ ℚ
